title: Add deterministic generator manifest, containment and additive CLI profile binding
goal: After GEN-VALVE-FOUNDATION-CORE-001 is merged, complete the second small foundation slice for issue #62: use the reviewed canonical input identity to add deterministic artifact manifest/hash plumbing, path-aware output containment and strictly additive optional profile binding in GeneratorCli while preserving the existing two-argument Motor CLI. Do not bind any real Valve interface fact.

prerequisite.rule: Do not dispatch this task until the core task implementation is merged to trusted main with green post-merge CI.

baselineEvidence.failedRun: Autonomous Agent run 36250733507 (#27) failed before candidate publication twice because the original combined task exceeded bounded coder steps. This task intentionally excludes compiler identity and Siemens name-policy implementation, which belong to its prerequisite core task.

scope: Use the already-reviewed CanonicalInputIdentity from the prerequisite task; do not reimplement or alter its semantics.

Add deterministic manifest plumbing in GeneratorCli. In profile-enabled mode the manifest contains a stable generator identity, canonical parsed-model input identity, the externally supplied opaque profile identity, and every generated PLC/source artifact as a relative path plus lowercase SHA-256 of exact bytes. Do not list/hash the manifest itself.
Manifest bytes must be deterministic with stable property/artifact ordering and no timestamp, absolute input/output path, locale, machine/user identity or other environment-dependent field.

Add path-aware output-root containment for every artifact and manifest before write. Reject rooted/absolute relative paths, parent traversal and sibling-prefix escapes. Use a separator-aware or Path.GetRelativePath-style containment proof; simple string-prefix StartsWith and substring-only '..' checks are not sufficient.

Keep the existing two-argument `GeneratorCli <input.json> <output-directory>` Motor flow compatible and still producing UDT_Motor.scl without requiring a profile token. Add profile/manifest behavior strictly additively, for example as an optional third opaque profile-identity argument.
Profile identity is opaque external binding only. Validate only bounded/safe representation needed for deterministic manifest transport; do not infer or fabricate Siemens library metadata.

Keep malformed/omitted JSON type tokens and unsupported AutomationType enum tokens fail-closed. Add stable bounded CLI diagnostic identity for parse/type/profile/containment failures without moving vendor-specific policy into Domain/PlcCompiler.

Add focused Linux tests for manifest determinism and hashes, profile-token separation from input identity, output containment including sibling-prefix/absolute/traversal attacks, malformed/omitted/unsupported type input, and legacy two-argument Motor compatibility.
Do not add any fbValve_Solenoid call, parameter, dependency/version, instance/data ownership, DB/memory or target prerequisite fact.

requirements: Candidate changes are limited exactly to candidatePolicy.allowedPaths and the prerequisite core identity/name-policy files are not modified.
Same parsed model plus same profile token produces byte-identical artifact bytes and manifest bytes across repeated Linux generation.
Changing only profile token changes manifest profile binding but does not change canonical parsed-model input identity.
Manifest contains stable generator/input/profile identities plus relative artifact path and lowercase SHA-256 for every generated PLC/source artifact, and does not include/hash itself.
Manifest/public output contains no timestamps, absolute input/output paths, locale, machine/user identity or environment-specific data.
Every output write is proven contained beneath output root before write; absolute, traversal and sibling-prefix escapes fail closed with stable diagnostics and write nothing outside root.
Existing two-argument Motor CLI remains supported without requiring a profile token and still produces UDT_Motor.scl.
Malformed/omitted required type tokens and unsupported enum tokens fail rather than defaulting semantics.
Focused Linux tests cover determinism, profile/input separation, hashes, containment attacks, input parse/type failures and legacy Motor CLI.
No unqualified Valve contract fact is asserted.
